sections.h2: How is Oregon laid out for someone selling a house?
sections.html:
Oregon covers 98,381 square miles, and where a house sits shapes almost everything about selling it, from the climate to the county office that handles the paperwork. Wikipedia describes eight regions: the coast, the Willamette Valley, the Rogue Valley, the Cascade Range, the Klamath Mountains, the Columbia Plateau, the High Desert and the Blue Mountains.

Most people live in the Willamette Valley, the stretch that runs from Eugene through Corvallis and Salem to Portland. The eastern two-thirds of the state is much more sparsely populated. A seller in Eugene and a seller in a High Desert town face the same state statutes, yet they deal with different county clerks, assessors and buyers.

The state had 4,237,256 residents at the 2020 census, up 10.6 percent from 2010, and it is made up of 36 counties and 241 incorporated cities. Salem is the capital.

sections.h2: Which Oregon cities are the largest?
sections.html:
Portland is by far the largest Oregon city, with 652,503 residents in the 2020 census, followed by Eugene and Salem at a little over 175,000 each. The list below uses the census figures as shown on Wikipedia.

Several of these cities cross a county line. Portland touches three counties, and Salem sits in both Marion and Polk, so the county that bills property tax and records the deed depends on the exact address.

Multnomah, Washington, Clackamas, Lane and Marion are the five most populous Oregon counties, and each has a county seat that houses the clerk and assessor.

  • Multnomah County, seat at Portland.
  • Washington County, seat at Hillsboro.
  • Clackamas County, seat at Oregon City.
  • Lane County, seat at Eugene.
  • Marion County, seat at Salem.

Size on the map is a different story. Harney County is the largest by area at 10,135 square miles, and Multnomah County is the smallest at 435 square miles. A rural parcel in Harney County and a bungalow in Multnomah County may share a statute, but the local office, the road access and the pool of likely buyers are very different.

sections.h2: What does the Oregon economy mean for home sellers?
sections.html:
Oregon's economy rests on a mix of technology, timber, agriculture and tourism, and which one dominates changes from region to region. Wikipedia credits the Silicon Forest, anchored by Intel and Tektronix, with making Intel the state's largest for-profit private employer. Nike is based in Beaverton and is the largest public company.

  • The state is the top lumber producer in the contiguous United States, though the timber industry has declined.
  • Oregon grows 95 percent of the nation's domestic hazelnuts, along with blueberries, wine grapes, cranberries and wheat.
  • Tourism draws on the mountains, forests and coast, including Mount Hood at 11,249 feet and Crater Lake.

Where a house sits in that mix can influence who is likely to buy it, and a Portland-area seller will meet a different market than one in farm country or the High Desert.

sections.h2: How is property tax run in Oregon?
sections.html:
Oregon property tax follows two ballot measures. Measure 5 caps taxes at $5 per $1,000 of real market value for education and $10 per $1,000 for general government, and Measure 50 limits how fast taxable value can grow. The county assessor sets values and the county tax collector bills and collects.

Measure 50 rolled each property's 1997-98 assessed value back to 90 percent of its 1995-96 value and called the result maximum assessed value. That figure can grow no more than 3 percent a year, and taxes are based on the lower of real market value or maximum assessed value. New construction, remodeling, new subdivisions and rezoning are exceptions. The Clackamas County explanation of Measures 5 and 50 covers the details.

Those dates come from Washington County, where statements are mailed on or before October 25. Late interest runs at 1.333 percent a month, starting on the 16th after a missed date. Other counties publish their own calendars on county websites, so confirm the date with your assessor and tax collector.

sections.h2: Does Oregon have a real estate transfer tax?
sections.html:
Generally no. ORS 306.815 bars cities, counties and other local bodies from taxing a transfer of real property, with exceptions that include a tax that was in effect on March 31, 1997.

Washington County does charge one. The county says the rate is $1 per $1,000 of the selling price, with liability shared between purchaser and seller. It must be paid, or an exemption filed, within 15 days of recording, and a late penalty applies after that. Exempt transfers include inheritances and gifts, deeds in lieu of foreclosure, transfers under $13,999, and trustee's deeds from foreclosure. See the county's exemption page.

A seller in Hillsboro or Beaverton should therefore ask about this tax at the start. Ask your title or escrow officer about any local transfer charge before you set a closing budget.

sections.h2: What disclosures does a seller owe in Oregon?
sections.html:
A seller of residential property must deliver a property disclosure statement to each buyer who makes a written offer, and the buyer has five days from delivery to revoke the offer unless that right is waived. The rules are in ORS 105.464 and the sections near it.

  • A seller who claims an exclusion completes only the first section of the form.
  • Listed exclusions include a first sale of a never-occupied dwelling, a sale by a financial institution after foreclosure or a deed in lieu, and sales by a court-appointed personal representative, trustee, conservator or guardian.
  • If the seller refuses to provide the form, the buyer may revoke at any time before closing.

Deeds and owner's sale agreements also carry a land use statement under ORS 93.040. It tells the buyer to confirm the lot is lawfully established, to learn the approved uses and, in the longer version used for owner's sale agreements, to check fire protection and farm and forest lawsuit limits. Transfer on death deeds are exempt from that statement.

sections.h2: What does Oregon weather and wildfire law mean for a house?
sections.html:
Western Oregon has an oceanic climate with very wet winters and dry summers, the Rogue Valley is Mediterranean with hotter summers, and the eastern two-thirds has cold, snowy winters and very dry summers. The record high is 119 degrees Fahrenheit and the record low is minus 54 degrees at Seneca.

On wildfire, the legislature voted in June 2025 to repeal the statewide wildfire hazard map. OPB reported that the bill also revoked the defensible space and building code requirements, with state agencies to write model codes that local governments may adopt. A 2023 law bars insurers from using a state-produced hazard map to cancel, decline to renew or raise premiums on a homeowner policy.

sections.h2: How do foreclosure, tax foreclosure and tenants work statewide?
sections.html:
Oregon counties can foreclose on a property for unpaid taxes once three years have passed from the earliest date of delinquency. Trust deed foreclosures follow separate rules, including a right to reinstate that must be exercised not later than five days before the last set sale date under ORS 86.778.

Tenants in a house sold at a foreclosure sale must get at least 30 days of written notice after the sale before being required to move, according to the notice form quoted in ORS 86.771. Each of those topics has its own guide on this site, and county practice differs on timing and court procedure.

faqs.q: How many counties and cities does Oregon have?
faqs.a: Oregon has 36 counties and 241 incorporated cities. Harney County is the largest county by area and Multnomah County is the smallest, though Multnomah has the largest population.

faqs.q: Does Oregon charge a state real estate transfer tax?
faqs.a: We found no state transfer tax in the sources we reviewed, and ORS 306.815 generally bars local transfer taxes. Washington County is a known exception, with a tax of $1 per $1,000 of the selling price that must be paid or exempted within 15 days of recording.

faqs.q: When are Oregon property taxes due?
faqs.a: November 15 is the due date for payment in full or for the first installment, with a 3 percent discount for paying in full. These dates are from Washington County, and other counties publish their own calendars.

faqs.q: Do I have to give a buyer a disclosure statement in Oregon?
faqs.a: Yes, in most residential sales. ORS 105.464 requires delivery to each buyer who makes a written offer, and the buyer has five days to revoke the offer after delivery. Some sellers, such as a bank after foreclosure or a court-appointed personal representative, qualify for an exclusion.

faqs.q: Is there still a statewide wildfire hazard map in Oregon?
faqs.a: No. The legislature voted in June 2025 to repeal the map, and the bill also revoked the defensible space and building code requirements in favor of model codes that local governments may adopt.
